content: A veggie burger is a type of hamburger specifically designed for vegetarians. The patty in a veggie burger can be crafted from a variety of ingredients, including vegetables, nuts, dairy products, mushrooms, textured vegetable protein (TVP), or a combination of these components. Some veggie burgers are vegan, but their availability can differ depending on geographic location or even between different branches of the same restaurant franchise. As of April 2005, veggie burgers were available at all Burger King restaurants, although they were not vegan. Certain Subway restaurants also offered veggie burgers. Additionally, many casual diners, often referred to as greasy spoon cafes, as well as high-end restaurants, include veggie burgers as a menu option. In countries like India, where vegetarianism is widely practiced, McDonald’s serves veggie burgers as one of their most popular menu items. Non-meat burger products from brands such as Boca, Gardenburger, and Morningstar Farms are widely distributed and sold in supermarkets across the United States. The first veggie burger was created in London in 1982 by Gregory Sams, who named it the VegeBurger. Gregory and his brother Craig had been operating a well-known natural food restaurant in Paddington since the 1960s. Following its launch, a Carrefour hypermarket in Southampton sold 2,000 packets of veggie burgers within three weeks, a success that was reported in The Observer newspaper on February 27, 1983.
